7427-toasts-and-forms-of-public-address-.creator: Unknown

arxiv-1912-04268.title: Eclipses of continuous gravitational waves as a probe of stellar structure
arxiv-1912-04268.creator: Pablo Marchant, Katelyn Breivik, Christopher P L Berry, Ilya Mandel, Shane L. Larson
arxiv-1912-04268.description: Abstract Although gravitational waves only interact weakly with matter, their propagation is affected by a gravitational potential. If a gravitational wave source is eclipsed by a star, measuring these perturbations provides a way to directly measure the distribution of mass throughout the stellar interior.

arxiv-1912-05036.title: RVSDG: An Intermediate Representation for Optimizing Compilers
arxiv-1912-05036.creator: Nico Reissmann, Jan Christian Meyer, Helge Bahmann, Magnus Själander
arxiv-1912-05036.description: Abstract Intermediate Representations (IRs) are central to optimizing compilers as the way the program is represented may enhance or limit analyses and transformations. Suitable IRs focus on exposing the most relevant information and establish invariants that different compiler passes can rely on.

arxiv-2012-11064.title: Data-Driven Geometric System Identification for Shape-Underactuated Dissipative Systems
arxiv-2012-11064.creator: Brian Bittner, Ross L. Hatton, Shai Revzen
arxiv-2012-11064.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Brian Bittner, Ross L. Hatton, Shai Revzen. Modeling system dynamics becomes challenging when the properties of individual system components cannot be directly measured, and often requires identification of properties from observed motion. In this paper, we show that systems whose movement is highly dissipative have features which provide an opportunity to more easily identify models and more quickly optimize motions than would be possible with general techniques.

arxiv-2103-05611.title: Optimal Pricing with a Single Point
arxiv-2103-05611.creator: Amine Allouah, Achraf Bahamou, Omar Besbes
arxiv-2103-05611.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Amine Allouah, Achraf Bahamou, Omar Besbes. We study the following fundamental data-driven pricing problem. How can/should a decision-maker price its product based on data at a single historical price? How valuable is such data? We consider a decision-maker who optimizes over (potentially randomized) pricing policies to maximize the worst-case ratio of the revenue she can garner compared to an oracle with full knowledge of the distribution of values, when the latter is only assumed to belong to a broad non-parametric set.

arxiv-2105-00885.title: Generating Extended Resolution Proofs with a BDD-Based SAT Solver (Extended Version)
arxiv-2105-00885.creator: Randal E. Bryant
arxiv-2105-00885.description: Abstract In 2006, Biere, Jussila, and Sinz made the key observation that the underlying logic behind algorithms for constructing Reduced, Ordered Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs) can be encoded as steps in a proof in the extended resolution logical framework. Through this, a BDD-based Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solver can generate a checkable proof of unsatisfiability.

arxiv-2202-05455.title: Deepest nodes in marked ordered trees
arxiv-2202-05455.creator: Helmut Prodinger
arxiv-2202-05455.description: Abstract . A variation of ordered trees, where each rightmost edge might be marked or not, if it does not lead to an endnode, is investigated. These marked ordered trees were introduced by E. Deutsch et al. to model skew Dyck paths. We study the number of deepest nodes in such trees.

arxiv-2207-10023.title: Tailoring Self-Supervision for Supervised Learning
arxiv-2207-10023.creator: WonJun Moon, Ji-Hwan Kim, Jae-Pil Heo
arxiv-2207-10023.description: Abstract Recently, it is shown that deploying a proper self-supervision is a prospective way to enhance the performance of supervised learning. Yet, the benefits of self-supervision are not fully exploited as previous pretext tasks are specialized for unsupervised representation learning. To this end, we begin by presenting three desirable properties for such auxiliary tasks to assist the supervised objective.

arxiv-2211-13988.title: Prospects of Probing Dark Matter Condensates with Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2211-13988.creator: and David F. Mota
arxiv-2211-13988.description: Abstract The Lambda-Cold Dark Matter model explains cosmological observations most accurately till date. However, it is still plagued with various shortcomings at galactic scales. Models of dark matter such as superfluid dark matter, Bose-Einstein Condensate(BEC) dark matter and fuzzy dark matter have been proposed to overcome some of these drawbacks.

arxiv-2307-01389.title: Identification of Causal Relationship between Amyloid- β \beta Accumulation and Alzheimer’s Disease Progression via Counterfactual Inference † \dagger These authors contributed equally to this paper. Corresponding author: Xiang Li (email: xli60@mgh.harvard.edu).
arxiv-2307-01389.creator: Haixing Dai † \dagger 1 , Mengxuan Hu † \dagger 1 , Qing Li † \dagger 2,3 , Lu Zhang 4 , Lin Zhao 1 , Dajiang Zhu 4 Ibai Diez 5 , Jorge Sepulcre 5 , Fan Zhang 6 , Xingyu Gao 7 , Manhua Liu 8 , Quanzheng Li 5 , Sheng Li 9 , Tianming Liu 1 , and Xiang Li 5
arxiv-2307-01389.description: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that is beginning with amyloidosis, followed by neuronal loss and deterioration in structure, function, and cognition. The accumulation of amyloid- β \beta in the brain, measured through 18F-florbetapir (AV45) positron emission tomography (PET) imaging, has been widely used for early diagnosis of AD.

arxiv-2310-12903.title: Homogenization of a nonlinear elliptic problem with imperfect rough interface
arxiv-2310-12903.creator: Sara Monsurrò, Carmen Perugia, Federica Raimondi
arxiv-2310-12903.description: Abstract This paper deals with an elliptic problem with a nonlinear lower order term set in an open bounded cylinder of ℝ N \mathbb{R}^{N} , N ≥ 2 N\geq 2 , divided into two connected components by an imperfect rough interface.

arxiv-2502-13464.title: Estimating Commonsense Plausibility through Semantic Shifts
arxiv-2502-13464.creator: Wanqing Cui, Keping Bi, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng
arxiv-2502-13464.description: Abstract Commonsense plausibility estimation is critical for evaluating language models (LMs), yet existing generative approaches–reliant on likelihoods or verbalized judgments–struggle with fine-grained discrimination. In this paper, we propose ComPaSS, a novel discriminative framework that quantifies commonsense plausibility by measuring semantic shifts when augmenting sentences with commonsense-related information.

arxiv-2505-05165.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous media equation
arxiv-2505-05165.creator: Roberta Bianchini, Min Jun Jo, Jaemin Park, Shan Wang
arxiv-2505-05165.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove the asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation near a stable stratified density, for initial perturbations in the Sobolev space H k H^{k} with any 2 < k ∈ ℝ 2<k\in\mathbb{R} .

arxiv-2509-16811.title: Prompt-Driven Agentic Video Editing System: Autonomous Comprehension of Long-Form, Story-Driven Media CCS: Human-centered computing Interactive systems and tools CCS: Computing methodologies Visual content-based indexing and retrieval CCS: Computing methodologies Video summarization CCS: Computing m
arxiv-2509-16811.creator: Zihan Ding, Xinyi Wang, Junlong Chen, Per Ola Kristensson, Junxiao Shen
arxiv-2509-16811.description: Abstract . Creators struggle to edit long-form, narrative-rich videos not because of UI complexity, but due to the cognitive demands of searching, storyboarding, and sequencing hours of footage. Existing transcript or embedding based methods fall short for video-editing workflows, as models struggle to track characters, infer motivations, and connect dispersed events.

arxiv-2510-02823.title: The Curious Case of In-Training Compression of State Space Models
arxiv-2510-02823.creator: Makram Chahine CSAIL, MIT Cambridge, MA 02139, USA chahine@mit.edu & Philipp Nazari ELLIS Institute Tübingen & Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems & Max Planck ETH Center for Learning Systems philipp.nazari@tuebingen.mpg.de and Daniela Rus CSAIL, MIT Cambridge, MA 02139, USA rus@csail.mit.e
arxiv-2510-02823.description: Abstract State Space Models (SSMs), developed to tackle long sequence modeling tasks efficiently, offer both parallelizable training and fast inference. At their core are recurrent dynamical systems that maintain a hidden state, with update costs scaling with the state dimension. A key design challenge is striking the right balance between maximizing expressivity and limiting this computational burden.

arxiv-2512-03369.title: FireSentry: A Multi-Modal Spatio-temporal Benchmark Dataset for Fine-Grained Wildfire Spread Forecasting DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: the 32th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 9 to 13, 2026; Jeju, Korea ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06
arxiv-2512-03369.creator: Nan Zhou, Huandong Wang, Jiahao Li, Han Li, Yali Song, Qiuhua Wang, Yong Li, Xinlei Chen
arxiv-2512-03369.description: Abstract . Fine-grained wildfire spread prediction is crucial for enhancing emergency response efficacy and decision-making precision. However, existing research predominantly focuses on coarse spatiotemporal scales and relies on low-resolution satellite data, capturing only macroscopic fire states while fundamentally constraining high-precision localized fire dynamics modeling capabilities.

pmc-10712946.title: Ryanodine receptor 2 inhibition reduces dispersion of cardiac repolarization, improves contractile function, and prevents sudden arrhythmic death in failing hearts
pmc-10712946.creator: Pooja Joshi, Shanea Estes, Deeptankar DeMazumder, Bjorn C Knollmann, Swati Dey, Olujimi A Ajijola, Pooja Joshi, Shanea Estes, Deeptankar DeMazumder, Bjorn C Knollmann, Swati Dey
pmc-10712946.description: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) from ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) is a leading cause of death, but current therapies are limited. Despite extensive research on drugs targeting sarcolemmal ion channels, none have proven sufficiently effective for preventing SCD. Sarcoplasmic ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) Ca2+ release channels, the downstream effectors of sarcolemmal ion channels, are underexplored in this context.

pmc-10751419.title: Ryanodine receptor type 1 content decrease‐induced endoplasmic reticulum stress is a hallmark of myopathies
pmc-10751419.creator: Jeremy Vidal, Eric A Fernandez, Martin Wohlwend, Pirkka‐Pekka Laurila, Andrea Lopez‐Mejia, Julien Ochala, Alexander J Lobrinus, Bengt Kayser, Isabel C Lopez‐Mejia, Nicolas Place, Nadège Zanou
pmc-10751419.description: BackgroundDecreased ryanodine receptor type 1 (RyR1) protein levels are a well‐described feature of recessive RYR1‐related myopathies. The aim of the present study was twofold: (1) to determine whether RyR1 content is also decreased in other myopathies and (2) to investigate the mechanisms by which decreased RyR1 protein triggers muscular disorders.

pmc-11354747.title: Melanin as a Photothermal Agent in Antimicrobial Systems
pmc-11354747.creator: Arianna Menichetti, Dario Mordini, Marco Montalti
pmc-11354747.description: Bacterial infection is one of the most problematic issues for human health and the resistance of bacteria to traditional antibiotics is a matter of huge concern. Therefore, research is focusing on the development of new strategies to efficiently kill these microorganisms. Recently, melanin is starting to be investigated for this purpose.

pmc-11634728.title: Aging research from bench to bedside and beyond: What we learned from Sammy Basso
pmc-11634728.creator: Giovanna Lattanzi, Chiara Lanzuolo, Eleonora Cugudda, Lorenzo Maggi, Luisa Politano, Olaya Santiago‐Fernández, Giulia Ricci, Stefano Squarzoni, Carlos Lopez‐Otin, the Italian Network for Laminopathies
pmc-11634728.description: ne of the most severe and life‐threatening accelerated aging diseases, affecting children shortly after birth (Cenni et al., 2020; Gordon et al., 2014). Yet, Sammy instead of succumbing to his condition, embraced it with remarkable resilience and a determination to make a difference.

pmc-12413164.title: Treatment of Secukinumab-induced Atopic Dermatitis-like Lesions Using Upadacitinib: A Case Report
pmc-12413164.creator: Wanyan Xiang, Xueping Lin, Qiuju Li, Wenjun Zheng
pmc-12413164.description: involving narrow-band ultraviolet B rays (NB-UVB) irradiation, halcinonide solution, and calcipotriol ointment failed to yield significant results. Subsequently, the patient underwent weekly Secukinumab therapy at 300 mg dosage, which led to complete control of his psoriasis (PASI0) within three weeks. However, post the fourth dose of Secukinumab, he noticed a small number of erythematic papules on his hands.

pmc-12625637.title: Pulmonary mucormycosis complicated by necrotizing pneumonia secondary to an obstructive endobronchial tumor-like lesion: a case report and review of literature
pmc-12625637.creator: Ngoc Duong-Minh, Khoa Nguyen-Dang
pmc-12625637.description: BackgroundMucormycosis is a rare but life-threatening invasive fungal infection, most commonly affecting immunocompromised individuals, especially those with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus. Pulmonary mucormycosis (PM) represents the second most frequent clinical form after rhino-orbital-cerebral disease and carries a high mortality rate. Diagnosis is often delayed because its clinical and radiological manifestations overlap with other pulmonary infections and malignancies.

pmc-13013882.title: SIRT3 activation protects from nabumetone-induced mitochondrial toxicity in adult human cardiomyocytes
pmc-13013882.creator: Yafei Huang, Hong Liu, Chao Tong, Zhimin Wang, Miaomiao Xu, Mengqi Dong, Rongjia Rao, Xianqiang Wang, Wei Feng, Zhan Hu, Fei Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Wang, Shengshou Hu, Bingying Zhou
pmc-13013882.description: Drug-induced mitochondrial toxicity is a major contributing factor to cardiotoxicity, which can cause drug attrition and adverse cardiac events. To assess the toxicity of anti-inflammatory agents, we used adult human primary cardiomyocytes (hPCMs) to screen 18 clinically available anti-inflammatory drugs in a high-content manner, and revealed widespread mitochondrial dysfunction without affecting cell viability.

pmc-13453288.title: Outcomes of Patients With Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma With Non-Clear Cell Histology Treated With Systemic Therapy
pmc-13453288.creator: Danielle Urman, Leah Deshler, Nicole Weise, Ahmed Shabaik, Ithaar Derweesh, Aditya Bagrodia, Brent Rose, Daniel Herchenhorn, Rana R. McKay
pmc-13453288.description: This study evaluated the outcomes of patients with non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and RCC with sarcomatoid features receiving systemic treatment. We conducted a single-center retrospective analysis of 251 patients with advanced RCC receiving systemic therapy. Overall, patients with nonclear cell histology and RCC with sarcomatoid features had worse overall survival compared to those with clear cell histology.

pmc-13674111.title: Comparison of outcomes after DA‐EPOCH‐R or GMALL high‐intensity therapy for front‐line treatment of Burkitt lymphoma: A retrospective cohort
pmc-13674111.creator: Eduard Schulz, Florian Posch, Kristina Friedrich, Peter Neumeister, Katharina T. Prochazka
pmc-13674111.description: In this retrospective cohort of adult Burkitt lymphoma, DA‐EPOCH‐R showed no signal of inferior survival or relapse risk compared with GMALL‐based high‐intensity therapy. Outcomes were driven mainly by established prognostic factors, particularly age, advanced stage and Burkitt lymphoma International Prognostic Index.

pmc-13685124.title: Parkinson’s disease LRRK2 mutations dysregulate iron homeostasis and promote oxidative stress and ferroptosis in human neurons and astrocytes
pmc-13685124.creator: Adamantios Mamais, Richard D Batchelor, Aravindraja Chairmandurai, Thomas B Ladd, Austin J Shute, Nitya Subrahmanian, Nunziata Maio, Christopher D Vulpe, Matthew J LaVoie
pmc-13685124.description: BackgroundIron accumulation is a hallmark of sporadic and familial Parkinson’s disease (PD) and correlates with clinical motor symptom severity. The biochemical mechanisms driving iron dyshomeostasis in PD brain and whether these are early or late events in the neurodegenerative process remain unknown.
